query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Using a data‐driven machine learning framework to screen the high-dimensional composition space of refractory HEAs will rapidly identify compositions with an improved combination of intrinsic strength, ductility, and lower density compared to those developed via traditional iterative thermo-kinetic methods.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional refractory high-entropy alloy formulations developed by slow, iterative thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation methods.
generation.intervention: Implement a machine learning model that is trained on high-throughput experimental and simulation data correlating elemental attributes (e.g., density, melting point, phase stability indicators) with mechanical properties.
generation.conditions: Screening within the multicomponent refractory alloy system under conditions relevant to high-temperature, high-performance applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Alloy composition‐driven microstructural features, including local lattice distortions and phase stability that mediate mechanical behavior.
generation.mechanism: The machine learning model leverages correlations between elemental properties and processing parameters to predict optimal compositions with reduced density while simultaneously achieving high intrinsic strength and ductility, thus bypassing the time‐consuming iterative design cycle.
generation.predicted_outcome: Rapid identification of RHEA compositions exhibiting improved tensile properties and lower weight relative to baseline alloys produced via traditional methods.
generation.baseline: RHEA compositions developed by established thermo‐kinetic and simulation approaches with longer iterative cycles and less optimal property combinations.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the machine learning model is expected to hold within the compositional regimes for which sufficient high-throughput data is available; predictions may be less reliable when extrapolating to regions with sparse data or extreme compositions.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of property improvements and the model's generalizability across all refractory systems are uncertain and will depend on the quality and representativeness of the training data.

falsification_experiment.design: Select two sets of RHEA alloy compositions: one set predicted by the machine learning framework and a control set developed via traditional iterative thermo-kinetic methods. Synthesize small batches of each alloy, ensuring similar processing histories, and perform mechanical testing (e.g., tensile tests) and density measurements under identical conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine learning-predicted alloys do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (e.g., higher tensile strength and elongation while maintaining lower density) compared to the control set at a predefined confidence level, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Materials with high performance both at room and elevated temperatures are very attractive for a wide range of critical applications, potentially for aero-engine and fusion reactors [1] – [4] . For decades, ultra-strong, ductile, and heat-resistant materials have long been sought by the materials community, such as tungsten-based heavy alloys and nickel-based superalloys [3] , [5] . However, achieving alloys with an ultrahigh strength (>2 GPa) and a sufficient ductility (>10%) has presented a long-standing challenge. This has spurred significant research into metallurgical strategies to tailor microstructures for improved properties. One classical design paradigm is utilizing dilute concentrations of alloying elements, such as Re, Ti, and Cr, to improve the properties of W-based alloys; however, the “strength-ductility trade-off” has proven to be difficult to be solved with such single principal-element alloy systems due to the problem of brittle W-enriched phases with body-centered cubic (bcc) structures [5] , [6] . The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

decision.trend: Early works in refractory high‐entropy alloys have largely relied on traditional synthesis and thermo‐kinetic simulations—using techniques such as spark plasma sintering, selective laser melting, magnetron sputtering, and controlled thermo‐mechanical treatments—to experimentally validate alloy performance. These studies progressively optimized properties like strength and ductility by carefully adjusting compositions and processing routes. However, the methods remain largely iterative and case‐specific, making it hard to rapidly screen the vast multicomponent composition space required for targeting additional constraints such as low weight.
decision.unsolved: A rapid and predictive design framework that can efficiently navigate the huge compositional landscape of refractory HEAs to directly pinpoint compositions that are simultaneously strong, ductile, and low‐weight is still lacking.
decision.lever: Develop a machine learning framework that leverages high‐throughput data (from both experiments and simulations) to correlate elemental attributes and processing parameters with the intrinsic mechanical properties and density. Key parameters would include elemental density, melting point, phase stability indicators, and microstructural features.
decision.why: This approach builds directly on prior work by shifting from slow, iterative thermo‐kinetic and simulation methodologies to a rapid, data‐driven screening method. It is well suited to addressing the complex, high‐dimensional design space of refractory HEAs and meets the demand for quick determination of optimal compositions.
